transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-08 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Kavita Rao (Redwood SE), Lee Park (Redwood CSM), Maria Chen (CTO, Nimbus), Darnell Price (Platform Eng), Elena Torres (Security), Samir Patel (Data Scientist)

00:00 Jordan: okay folks, thanks for joining on short notice, want to run through the weekly POC check, access state and the bench numbers we ran overnight. Kavita, do you want to start with the infra/access updates?
00:18 Kavita: yeah sure. Quick note — we verified the VPC peering was established, there was a small firewall rule for egress to our control plane, it was blocking metrics so we flipped that, should be good now. Maria, you should see agent heartbeats in the console.
00:33 Maria: yep I can see the heartbeat indicator, it just showed up. there was a little delay earlier, thought something hung on our side.
00:40 Darnell: we also updated the route tables per the runbook, i left a note in the ticket, but we did see some packet drops on one AZ while we were testing. might be transient.
00:50 Kavita: that transient drop may explain a couple of the higher tail latencies in the benchmark — i'll show the breakdown in a minute.
01:02 Jordan: great, thanks. Lee anything on onboarding or credentials?
01:08 Lee: yes, SSO test user provisioned, instructions in shared drive (drive.google.com/nimbus/pilot-ssotest). we still need the final SAML cert exchange though.
01:18 Elena: we have the cert, we just need Redwood to confirm fingerprint format, our IdP's cert helper munges line breaks sometimes so the metadata gets malformed.
01:29 Kavita: got it, we'll send the exact fingerprint string, i'll embed it in the email.
01:36 Jordan: moving to bench results — Kavita, walk us through the 5k requests job from last night.
01:43 Kavita: sure. We ran a 5000 request simulated storefront scenario over a 10 minute window. default config: batch size 8, dynamic batching enabled, prefix KV cache warm. Observed avg token latency ~65ms, P95 ~210ms, P99 ~480ms. throughput ended up around 220 tokens/sec per GPU instance with our quantized model variant.
02:08 Samir: wait, 480 at P99 seems high vs what we expected, we were hoping to be <300. what causes that spike?
02:16 Kavita: two main reasons. One: a small number of requests hit a cold KV cache due to eviction during the run — our eviction policy was set to aggressive to save memory. Two: there's a tail caused by network retransmits in that AZ where Darnell saw packet drops. So it's a mix of infra noise and cache misses.
02:34 Maria: can we quantify cache hit-rate?
02:38 Kavita: yes — overall hit-rate was ~88% but in the 3rd minute it dropped to ~62% when eviction swept. that's visible in the bench CSV I attached to the ticket.
02:48 Samir: ok that explains it. If we bump cache size or change eviction threshold we should see P99 come down.
02:54 Kavita: absolutely. I tested increasing cache retention from 200MB to 600MB in a quick config and reran a smaller 1k run — P99 dropped to ~260ms, P95 to ~160ms. average stayed similar.
03:08 Darnell: what's the memory tradeoff per GPU? will that block other workloads?
03:13 Kavita: estimated extra 400MB per worker — on Dedicated it's fine but on shared Hosted tier we have to watch density. We can also trade by lowering batch size but that impacts throughput.
03:24 Jordan: so it's a latency vs cost/density tradeoff, which is expected. Maria — what is your target P95 and P99 for the pilot?
03:33 Maria: we want P95 under 200ms for personalized recs, P99 ideally under 300ms. It's not firm for all calls but for user-facing recs it needs to be consistent.
03:44 Jordan: ok good, that's actionable. Kavita, can you produce a tuned config to aim for P99 <300 with reasonable memory?
03:50 Kavita: yes — i'll share two profiles: conservative (bigger cache) and cost-saver (smaller cache + lower batch) with expected numbers and token/sec.
03:58 Lee: i'll include expected cost delta in the note so Maria's team can compare.
04:05 Elena: from security side — the audit logs for inference requests, are they stored in our control plane or in Nimbus's logging? We need to ensure no PII is retained.
04:17 Kavita: by default logs are in Redwood's control plane for hosted, but for this pilot we pushed logs to Nimbus's S3 via the connector you configured. We support redaction and request-level anonymization — you had opt-in.
04:30 Elena: ok good, can you share the redaction config? we want to validate against our DLP.
04:36 Jordan: we'll share the redaction rules doc (link: drive.google.com/nimbus/redaction), Kavita will also include example logs.
04:44 Darnell: another infra question — if we move to Dedicated reserved capacity, will we still get prefix cache persistence across restarts or is that ephemeral?
04:54 Kavita: Dedicated gives you more control — we support persistent KV for dedicated pools, but it requires a config toggle and extra storage. For hosted it's ephemeral. We'll include the exact option and storage cost estimate.
05:06 Maria: what's the timeline to enable persistent KV for our pool?
05:09 Kavita: it's a config flip plus a small migration step; we can do it in the pilot window, estimate 2-3 business days to provision.
05:16 Jordan: good. moving on: network triage — Darnell, you saw packet drops in AZ-b, can you summarize?
05:23 Darnell: during the bench we saw 0.6% packet retransmit spikes between 02:10–02:13 which aligned with tail spikes. seems like an intermittent switch issue, ops already scheduled a ticket with cloud provider.
05:35 Kavita: we can re-run benches in a different AZ to isolate infra vs infra + model behavior. suggest we run three runs across AZ-a and AZ-c in the next window.
05:45 Maria: yes please do that. Also can Redwood include a run that mimics higher concurrent small requests (burst traffic), not just steady state?
05:55 Kavita: yes — we can do a 5k burst test vs 10 minute steady test — i'll include both.
06:04 Samir: for our metric collection — can you add a request-level tag for experiment id so we can map rec latency to user cohort?
06:12 Kavita: yes we'll include experiment_id header.
06:15 Jordan: okay, next — rollout/rollback and canary plan. Maria, you asked earlier about runbook ownership?
06:22 Maria: right, we need a clear owner for rollback steps if a canary hurts latency or quality. We prefer Nimbus to own traffic cutover but Redwood to own model fallback and quick patching.
06:33 Jordan: that's reasonable. we'll draft a joint runbook where Nimbus handles traffic routing and Redwood has a one-click fallback to a lower-capacity model variant. we'll add alert thresholds at P95 and error-rate.
06:45 Elena: please include which logs are forwarded to our SIEM and the retention period before deletion.
06:50 Lee: we'll list retention and redaction options.
06:54 Kavita: on quality — we saw a slight perplexity bump in the second run, likely due to a different tokenizer shard mapping; we believe it's noise but we'll re-run with deterministic tokenizer seed to confirm.
07:08 Samir: if deterministic seed changes output distribution, we need to mark that in evals, might affect A/B.
07:14 Kavita: agreed. i'll annotate the eval spreadsheets.
07:18 Jordan: any blockers for gating to the next phase? Maria?
07:22 Maria: main blockers: final SAML cert exchange, the SOC2 scoping questions answered, and a stable P99 <300 in the next bench across two AZs. Also pricing estimate for Dedicated burst.
07:35 Jordan: those are clear. We'll prioritize SAML fingerprint and the tuned config.
07:40 Kavita: action: i'll run multi-AZ benches and the burst test Monday and share CSVs.
07:46 Darnell: once you share CSVs, i'll correlate with our network telemetry to confirm infra vs model.
07:52 Jordan: perfect. quick note — competitor question: Maria asked whether Anthropic endpoints would be a fallback option. Maria?
07:59 Maria: just checking options; not necessary now but we want to know if Redwood supports falling back to another model provider if capacity dries up.
08:08 Kavita: we support fallback to Redwood-verified variants and partner endpoints with routing policies; we'll document compatible models and cost differences.
08:18 Jordan: closing — recap of next steps and owners. Kavita will share tuned configs and bench CSV by 2026-01-11; Jordan will send Dedicated burst cost estimate by 2026-01-12; Lee to enable SSO test user and instructions immediate; Elena to send SOC2 scoping questions by 2026-01-14.
08:38 Maria: that works. thank you.
08:42 Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links and schedule the latency deep-dive for next week if needed.
08:50 [meeting ends]

Notes on transcript: occasional transcription errors — "K-V cash" instead of KV cache, "perplexity" may be misheard as "perfectly" in one clip. Speaker attribution auto-labeled in spots as Speaker 4 where name mapping ambiguous.
